newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal declares state of calamity in Azores.
newsitem.headline: Portugal declares state of calamity in Azores.

text.p: The Portuguese government on Friday approved two billion escudos ($13 million) of emergency aid for the Azores Islands and declared a state of calamity in the storm-battered mid-Atlantic archipelago.
The declaration clears the way for the islands, which were lashed by violent storms over Christmas, to seek financial help from the European Union.

The storms, in which winds gusted up to 95 miles (150 km) per hour, damaged harbours, houses and roads. Nobody was seriously hurt but a number of families were forced to flee their homes by flood waters.
The port of Ponta Delgada, the islands' capital, stayed closed on Friday as divers and salvage operators sought to clear cables and sunken containers that posed a danger to shipping.
The port's quay was seriously battered by boats that broke free of their moorings during the gales which whipped up heavy seas.
Local government officials have put the total damage caused by storms over the past month at around 10 billion escudos ($66 million).
